Q-PO-01.text: Once your system is in use, do you regularly check whether its inputs or its performance have changed?
Q-PO-01.expectedPractice: Once the system is in use, a named person checks on a set schedule whether its inputs and its performance have moved away from what it was tested on. You record the checks, their thresholds and who acts when a threshold is crossed.
Q-PO-01.whyAsked: Data changes with seasons, new clinics, new phones and new policies; a model nobody watches gets worse unnoticed, often until it harms the people it serves.
evidenceExamples: the monitoring plan
a link to the dashboard or check script
the C-21 notebook summary used to set thresholds

answerLabels.not_applicable: It will never be used outside the study

answerPrompts.done: Say what is checked, how often, the thresholds, who acts, by role, and where the plan is kept; it prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.partly: Say which checks, thresholds and roles are set so far and which are still open; it prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.not_yet: If the system is not in use yet, say so; say what you plan to check and when. It prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.not_applicable: Say why the system will never be used outside the study; it prints in the model card.

Q-PO-01.practiceSameAsReason: Every element, condition and example of 5.1.0's practice is kept, reworded in the second person; 5.1.0's expectedPractice equals 5.0.0's.

Q-PO-02.text: Have you written down when and how your model is retrained?
Q-PO-02.expectedPractice: You record what triggers retraining, such as a monitored measure crossing your threshold, a change in the population served or a set date; the steps to retrain and check the new model; and who decides, by role.
Q-PO-02.whyAsked: Without agreed triggers and written steps, a worsening model runs on, or is retrained and used unchecked.
evidenceExamples: the retraining procedure
the monitoring plan with its thresholds
the record of a past retraining

answerLabels.partly: Partly, some of it is written

answerPrompts.done: Name the triggers and your thresholds, the steps, who decides, by role, and where it is recorded; it prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.partly: Name the triggers, steps and roles set so far and what is still open; it prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.not_yet: Say when you will set the triggers and steps, and whether the system is in use yet; it prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.not_applicable: Say why your model will never be retrained; it prints in the model card.

Q-PO-03.text: Can a person review and override your system's outputs before they are acted on?
Q-PO-03.expectedPractice: Users can review each output before it is acted on, or a sample in proportion to the risk, and override it. Your written rules on how to override, who may do it, by role, and how overrides are recorded are in use.
Q-PO-03.whyAsked: A person who can check and override the system catches errors before they cause harm, if overriding is clear and used.
evidenceExamples: the workflow showing the review step
a log or summary of overrides
the user guide section on overriding

answerLabels.not_applicable: Review by a person does not apply

Q-PO-04.expectedPractice: You record who is responsible, by role and organisation, for each part of the system's outcomes, including deciding to deploy it, monitoring, responding to harm, fixing errors and deciding to stop it, and each role holder agreed.
Q-PO-04.whyAsked: When organisations share a system, harms go unaddressed if each thinks another is responsible; named roles say who acts.

Q-PO-05.text: Have you written an incident response plan for when your system causes harm?
Q-PO-05.expectedPractice: You have a written plan for when the system causes or may cause harm. It says how a problem is reported, who is alerted, by role, how the system is paused or limited, how the people affected are told and helped, and how the cause is found and fixed.
Q-PO-05.whyAsked: Harm from a system in use needs a fast response that planning in the moment cannot give; a written plan shows the people affected that you take problems seriously.
evidenceExamples: the incident response plan
the record of an exercise or a real incident
the contact route shown to users

Q-PO-06.expectedPractice: You train or guide the people who use the system's outputs, in a language and form that suits them, on what outputs mean, how far to trust them, when not to rely on them and how to report a problem.
Q-PO-06.whyAsked: Users who misunderstand a system trust it too much or ignore it; short, practical training is often the cheapest safeguard.

Q-PO-07.text: Can your users understand each output, how confident it is and its limits?
Q-PO-07.expectedPractice: Your system shows users each output with how confident it is and the main limits that apply, in words they understand, and you checked that users read them correctly. In proportion to the risk, where an output is about a person, the user can see its main reasons. Telling stakeholders the limits in general is a separate question.
Q-PO-07.whyAsked: An output users misread is as harmful as a wrong one; seeing the confidence and the reasons lets a user decide when to question the system.
evidenceExamples: screenshots of the output screen
results of testing with users

Q-PO-16.whyAsked: Real use shows problems that testing missed; starting small limits who is affected while you find them.
